metadata.note: The Texas and Pacific Railway, chartered by Congress March 3, 1871 to build a southern transcontinental line from Marshall, Texas to San Diego. It never got west of El Paso: the Southern Pacific built east ahead of it, and the Gould-Huntington Agreement of November 26, 1881 stopped the T&P at Sierra Blanca, 92 miles short, with joint use of SP track into El Paso. The main line is modelled as three cumulative features with non-overlapping year ranges (1873-1875, 1876-1880, 1881-1971) so the slider shows it building westward; they are the same physical railroad, not parallel routes. The Louisiana arm (Shreveport-Alexandria-New Orleans, completed September 12, 1882) already exists as tp-shreveport-new-orleans in shreveport_railroads.geojson, and tp-longview-shreveport here is the connector that joins it to the main line at Longview. NOT INCLUDED: the Trans-Continental Division (Texarkana-Paris-Sherman-Fort Worth, opened in stages 1873-1881) - most of it is abandoned, parts are now the Northeast Texas Trail, and its intermediate alignment could not be verified well enough to trace. Geometry is real OSM track; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from timetables. Dates are sourced to the Handbook of Texas (TSHA) and Wikipedia.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The 66-mile Longview-Waskom-Shreveport line was the T&P's only predecessor in Texas that had actually built and operated a railroad; acquired March 21, 1872, per the Handbook of Texas.

properties.line: Texas and Pacific: Texarkana – Fort Worth

segments.note: approx.; the line was extended from Eagle Ford (Dallas) to Fort Worth on July 19, 1876, giving the T&P 444 miles of line. Attempts to finance further construction toward the Pacific failed until Jay Gould's syndicate took an interest in the fall of 1879.

properties.line: Texas and Pacific: Texarkana – El Paso

segments.note: Track laying resumed at Fort Worth April 1, 1880 under Grenville Dodge and reached Sierra Blanca December 16, 1881 - 520 miles. The Gould-Huntington Agreement of November 26, 1881 stopped the T&P there, 92 miles short of El Paso, and gave the two systems joint use of the Southern Pacific line into El Paso, forming a continuous route to the Pacific. Headway approximate.

segments.note: approx.; the Sunshine Special, inaugurated December 5, 1915, was the MP/T&P flagship - St. Louis to Texas, with Dallas, Fort Worth and El Paso cars cut out at Longview or Marshall and forwarded over the T&P, per Wikipedia.

segments.note: approx.; the diesel streamliner Texas Eagle displaced the Sunshine Special into a secondary role in August 1948; the last unnamed vestige of the Sunshine Special left MP timetables in 1962.
